finding.claim: Reflected XSS and local-variable disclosure on the debug traceback page: exception messages and frame locals are rendered unescaped when debug or testing is enabled.
finding.source: Request-derived data that reaches an exception message or frame local, e.g. int(request.args['n']) whose ValueError message echoes the raw input.
finding.sink: debug.py:59 {{ value }}, :72 {{ line }}, :80 {{ repr }} rendered into an HTML 500 response via Template(TEMPLATE) with no autoescape (debug.py:112-113).

trace.note: re-raises the original exception when propagate is true
render(value=error, frames=...) passes the exception and frame locals

finding.guards_checked: No |e/escape/Markup in TEMPLATE. Jinja Template defaults to autoescape=False (jinja2/environment.py:1186). Traceback page only served when app.debug or app.testing; non-debug responses use the generic 500 path. Applies only with debug/testing enabled in a deployed app.

finding.claim: Chunked (no Content-Length) multipart/form-data upload bypasses MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH, letting an unauthenticated client write unbounded file data to disk and grow memory for text fields, limited only by bandwidth within BODY_TIMEOUT.
finding.source: Unauthenticated POST with multipart/form-data and Transfer-Encoding: chunked (no Content-Length header).
finding.sink: Streaming file parts to stream_factory storage (formparser.py:173-178, 208-209, 216) and accumulating text-field chunks in memory (formparser.py:202-204, 216).

trace.note: Body precheck only sets _must_raise when Content-Length is present and exceeds the limit
parse iterates body via async for, which uses Body.__anext__
Body.__anext__ streams chunks with no cumulative size check
the only cumulative MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH check is in __await__, which the multipart path does not use
MultipartDecoder receives max_content_length as max_form_memory_size, which werkzeug enforces only per incoming chunk (werkzeug/sansio/multipart.py:136-147)
start_file_streaming writes file parts to stream_factory with no total cap

finding.guards_checked: Content-Length precheck (request.py:65-70) covers only non-chunked bodies. MAX_FORM_MEMORY_SIZE 500KB (formparser.py:211-214) applies only to non-file fields. MAX_FORM_PARTS 1000 caps part count. BODY_TIMEOUT 60s (request.py:359) bounds parse duration. Urlencoded bodies are safe because they use __await__ (request.py:102-106).

finding.claim: url_for(_external=True) builds absolute URLs from the request Host header when SERVER_NAME is unset, so application-generated links (e.g. password-reset emails) can point to an attacker-chosen host. Informational, app-level pattern rather than a framework defect.
finding.source: Host header supplied by the client on the request.
finding.sink: Absolute URL generated by url_for(..., _external=True) for links sent to users or used in redirects.

trace.note: create_url_adapter builds subdomain from request when request is present
host = request.host.lower() when server_name is None
host mismatch only emits a warning and sets subdomain to <invalid>; URL still built from Host

finding.guards_checked: SERVER_NAME config (app.py:244) fixes the host when set. routing.py:63-69 warns on mismatch but does not block. Only exploitable if the app builds externally visible links from url_for without setting SERVER_NAME.
